q: 1. Which operation must complete first?
options: right of the line joining two circles
left of the line joining two circles
explain: In network logic, progress moves from left to right; therefore, activities on the left must be completed before those on the right.

q: 2. A drawback of bar chart is
options: it is difficult to judge whether an activity is completed or not
all the activities represented are independent of each other
sequence of activities is not clearly defined
it is not possible to judge whether the activity is ahead or behind the schedule.
explain: The critical limitation of a standard bar chart is that it does not show logical dependency linkages or critical activity sequences.

q: 3. In PERT, the critical path represents the
options: shortest path for the earliest completion of the project
longest path of the network from the initial to final event
ideal path by proceeding along which the project can be completed as per schedule
path which takes into account the completion of the parallel activities
explain: The critical path is defined as the longest path through the network from start to finish, determining minimum project duration.

q: 4. Zero float for any activity means that the activity is
explain: Zero float (zero slack) means the activity has no spare time and lies exactly on the critical path, making it critical.

q: 5. The interrelationship between the functional elements of a programme is achieve through
explain: A work breakdown structure shows how the elements of a programme relate.

q: 6. Which of the following is a PERT event?
explain: An event is a milestone (a completion). The other options are ongoing activities.

q: 7. In PERT analysis, the start and end of event is represented by
explain: Per the answer key, b (event).

q: 8. When all the paths are arranged according to the descending order of the float, the path which is next to the critical path is known as
explain: The path with the second-lowest amount of float (next to the critical path, which has zero float) is technically referred to in this context as the semi-critical path.

q: 9. Which of the following does not represent an activity?
options: The office area is being cleaned
explain: 'Site located' is a completed state (an event). The rest are ongoing tasks.

q: 10. PERT is
explain: PERT is event oriented, since its network is analysed in terms of events.

q: 11. Completion of an activity on CPM network, is generally known
explain: In CPM networks, the point of completion (or start) of an activity is represented as a node.

q: 12. When the events are numbered in a network then the number of the head event of an activity is
options: always larger than the number of the tail event of same activity
always smaller than the number of the tail event of the same activity
always equal to the number of the tail event of the same activity
explain: By Fulkerson's rule, the head event number is always greater than the tail event number.

q: 13. The estimated time required to perform an activity, is known as
explain: Duration is the estimated time needed to complete an activity.

q: 14. PERT means
options: pertinent programming related to a project
explain: PERT is the standard acronym for Program Evaluation and Review Technique.

q: 15. For completion of a project, the critical path of the network represents
explain: The critical path determines the minimum time in which the entire project can be completed.

q: 16. You are going to design a new computer programme, which would you like to prefer?
explain: Software development involves high uncertainty in task durations, making the probabilistic PERT method more suitable than deterministic CPM.

q: 17. Which of the following is an example of parallel activities?
options: Construction of walls and casting of roof
Construction of walls and carpentry work of doors and window
Casting of roof and construction of septic tank
Digging of well and construction of septic tank
explain: Per the answer key, b. Wall construction and door/window carpentry can proceed at the same time.

q: 18. The optimistic time estimate represents
options: the shortest time required to complete the activity under favorable conditions
the maximum time required to complete the activity under adverse conditions
the time the activity would most often require if normal conditions prevail
explain: Optimistic time is the shortest time if everything goes well.

q: 19. The square root of the variance is known as
explain: By definition, the standard deviation is the square root of the variance.

q: 20. The variance of the PERT critical path is equal to
options: sum of variance of activities lying on critical path
maximum of sum of variances upto end event
minimum of sum of variances upto end event
explain: The variance of the project completion time equals the sum of the variances of all activities lying on the critical path.

q: 21. Higher standard deviations means
explain: A larger standard deviation means a wider spread of possible times, so more uncertainty.

q: 22. Slack is given as the difference between
options: latest allowable time and earliest expected time
latest allowable time and the pessimistic time estimate
earliest expected time and latest allowable time
final event time and initial event time
explain: Slack = TL – TE.

q: 23. For all the events along the critical path, the slack is
explain: Critical events have the minimum slack, usually zero.

q: 24. A dummy activity in a network
options: is represented by a dotted line
does not consume time or resources
explain: A dummy is an artificial activity drawn as a dotted arrow that takes no time or resources.

q: 25. In the critical path of construction planning, free float can be
explain: Per the answer key, c. Free float is never greater than total float, and is at least the independent float.

q: 26. Higher standard deviations means
explain: In PERT, standard deviation measures the dispersion of possible completion times; a higher value indicates a wider range of possibilities and thus greater uncertainty.

q: 27. If D is the duration, ES and EF are the earlist start and earliest finish time, LS and LF are latest start and latest finish time, then following relation holds good
explain: All given basic scheduling relationships mathematically link activity duration to early and late start/finish times[cite: 1].

q: 28. Probability factor is
explain: The probability factor (Z-score) in PERT is defined as (T_s - T_E) / \sigma[cite: 1].

q: 29. If σ1, σ2, σ3, .........are the standard deviations of completion for the activities along the critical path, the standard deviations of the time of completion of the project is given by
explain: The project standard deviation is the square root of the sum of the variances ($\sigma^2$) of the activities on the critical path.

q: 30. Slack is
options: difference of latest allowable time and earliest expected time
explain: Slack is defined as the difference between the latest allowable time and the earliest expected time of an event.

q: 31. Critical path
explain: The critical path is always the longest path in the network.

q: 32. For the preparation of construction schedule, the data required is
explain: Preparing a construction schedule requires data on operations, activities, and labour output - all these inputs are needed.

q: 33. Milestone chart is an improvement over
explain: Milestone charts improve on bar charts by marking key events.

q: 34. An activity requires
explain: An activity needs time and resources.

q: 35. The optimistic time represent the
options: shortest possible time in which an activity can be completed if everything goes exceptionally well
time in which the activity is normally expected to complete under normal contingencis
time in which an activity will take to complete in case of difficulty
explain: That is the definition of optimistic time.

q: 36. The time in which an activity will take to complete in case of difficulty, is called
explain: That is the definition of pessimistic time.

q: 37. When all the paths are arranged according to the descending order of the float, the path which is next to critical path is known as
explain: Per the answer key, semi-critical path.

q: 38. Fulkerson's rule is used for numbering the
explain: Fulkerson's rule numbers the events so that each head number exceeds its tail number.

q: 39. A construction schedule is prepared after collecting
explain: Scheduling requires comprehensive data on task quantities, labor productivity (output), and machinery capacity to determine durations.

q: 40. An important assumption in PERT calculations is:
explain: PERT assumes individual activity times are statistically independent of each other, which allows summing their variances along the critical path.

q: 41. PERT stands for
options: Pertinent equation related to a task
explain: PERT stands for Programme Evaluation and Review Technique.

q: 42. In PERT analysis, the time estimates of activities and probability of their occurrence follow
explain: Per the answer key, a. Note: PERT normally assumes the beta distribution (c).

q: 43. Time estimated time required to complete an activity is termed as
explain: The time needed to complete an activity is its duration.
